terms.grammar: comparative adverb (“more swiftly”), with an imperative

phrases.english: Hurry up, why are you standing there?

phrases.latin: heus Phaedrōme, exī, exī, exī, inquam, ōcius.
phrases.english: Hey, Phaedromus, come out, out, out, I say, quick!

sources: Lewis & Short: propero · Lewis & Short: ocior

Plautus, Terence and Cicero’s letters checked against the Perseus Latin texts (Plautus ed. Leo, with its line numbers; Terence ed. Parry, whose line numbers can run one off the OCT’s; lines taken from the loci collections are cited by the OCT’s; Cicero’s letters ed. Purser).
Lines marked as in the Latinitas loci collections (loci-plautus, loci-terentius, loci-cicero-epistulae and others) are quoted from them.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 67, 101, 108, 330.
